findings.reason: naming the existing remote-anchored read and its three-valued answer changes which function the node calls and what it does when the question cannot be asked, which is otherwise left to the implementer's default.
findings.text: the deliverable requires "every run of that section that has delivered or been promoted has its head reachable from the primary branch" but names neither the module nor the mechanism that answers it, while reckon already ships `merge.head_on_remote_branch` (`reckon/crew/merge.py:662`), which reads the REMOTE primary branch and returns `on_branch` as True, False or **None** (`unreachable`, `missing-branch`, `no-remote`); the repo has already measured that a head on the local checkout's main but not pushed is not on the primary branch (tests/test_a_plain_complete_refuses_an_unmerged_head.py), so a node that answers with a local `merge-base --is-ancestor` passes this plan's own test — where the merge is local — and then holds waiters indefinitely for work landed from another clone, and the two-valued rule has no stated answer for `on_branch is None`, where release-early repeats the reported defect and hold-on-unknown stalls every waiter on an unreadable remote

findings.reason: without a case for it the unmeasured half of the deliverable ships as today's behaviour, and the node would close on a gate that cannot see it.
findings.text: the deliverable holds a wait while any run of the section "has delivered or been promoted" and is unlanded, but all three cases exercise only promoted runs, so a node that implements the promoted branch from the ledger's recorded revisions satisfies the done-when while a run that finished and was never promoted (a live pointer at phase `complete`, which the ticker counts as `unpromoted`) still releases the waiter on the declaration alone — the same defect on the other population, and one whose enumeration source (live pointers) is a different read from the promoted one (ledger rows), so passing the suite says nothing about it
